page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.12xlarge is a high-performance computing instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 24 physical cores and 24 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz with one thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 32.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or graphics processing units, but features a baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (specifically avx512f, avx512_vnni, and avx512_bf16) alongside SHA_NI and AES cryptography extensions.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidth testing in the top 10% tier. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU evaluations, alongside Geekbench and Passmark CPU scores, consistently place in the top 25% tier. The instance demonstrates average performance in single-threaded gzip compression, static web serving throughput, and large-model LLM inference. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Passmark database operations perform in the top 25% tier, reflecting the efficiency of the dedicated core allocation and high-speed DDR5 memory architecture.

From a resource density perspective, the hpc7a.12xlarge offers a high memory-to-core ratio of 32 GB per core, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound parallel workloads that do not require local storage. The lack of bundled local NVMe storage represents a tradeoff, requiring external network storage for persistent data. This instance is suited for memory-intensive high-performance computing workloads, scientific simulations, database operations, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
